subject.title: fix(gateway): force exit on zombie shutdown + 503 healthz during shutdown

question: Should the terminal Gateway daemon permanently expose a five-second forced-exit watchdog and the `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_POST_SHUTDOWN_EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS` override as its shutdown-recovery contract?
rationale: The patch can mechanically implement either policy, but choosing an operator-visible environment surface and intentionally terminating a process after clean teardown is a gateway lifecycle and support-policy decision.

options.title: Adopt the watchdog contract
options.body: Keep the terminal-daemon-only watchdog, document the timeout and invalid-value fallback, and require PR-head supervisor-recovery proof before merge.

options.title: Use a fixed internal timeout
options.body: Keep the availability safeguard but remove the new environment override to avoid expanding the operator configuration surface.

options.title: Pause forced termination
options.body: Retain the strict internal probe work separately and defer process-exit policy until gateway owners define the recovery contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt the watchdog contract
recommendation.body: Keep the terminal-daemon-only watchdog, document the timeout and invalid-value fallback, and require PR-head supervisor-recovery proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is gateway lifecycle product policy, and the PR timeline shows this person was explicitly brought into that discussion.
